AI MarTech to Triple to $74B, Birdeye Ships 27 AI Coworkers, 79% Face Adoption Challenges

Today's top stories in AI + enterprise tech

AI MarTech Market to Nearly Triple to $74.3B by 2031

New market report shows AI MarTech growing from $28B in 2025 to $74.3B by 2031 at 17.66% CAGR. The drivers: agentic AI, platform consolidation, and privacy-first personalization. Enterprises are consolidating marketing tech across data, identity, content, orchestration, and analytics — creating demand for integrated AI platforms that connect campaign decisions with customer outcomes.

Birdeye Deploys 27 "AI Coworkers" Named Jay, Myna, and Robin

Customer experience platform Birdeye announced deployment of 27 autonomous AI coworkers — specialized personas designed to manage complex marketing and customer service workflows. The naming convention (bird-themed: Jay, Myna, Robin) signals a shift from "AI tools" to "AI teammates" with distinct personalities and roles. This is the agentic workforce becoming real.

Writer Survey: 79% Face AI Adoption Challenges Despite High Investment

Writer's 2026 enterprise AI adoption survey reveals a stark reality: 97% deployed AI agents, but only 29% see significant ROI. The kicker? 67% of executives believe they've already suffered a data breach from unapproved AI tools. And 75% admit their AI strategy is "more for show" than actual guidance. The gap between deployment and transformation is widening.

Adobe: 68% of Marketers Are "Disconnected" From AI Strategy

Adobe's CX AI Maturity Index categorizes enterprise marketers by their ability to scale and control AI-powered experiences. The verdict: 68% are "Disconnected" — using AI in silos without repeatable systems or shared governance. Only 15% qualify as "Orchestrated" with connected, controlled, continuously optimized AI across channels. The path forward: clear ownership and systematic integration.

Enterprise AI Market to Hit $206.6B by 2031

The broader enterprise AI market is projected to grow from $40.7B in 2025 to $206.6B by 2031 — a 31.7% CAGR driven by cloud infrastructure and agentic AI adoption. While marketing represents a slice of this, the infrastructure investments are creating the foundation for AI-native marketing stacks. The companies building data readiness now will capture this wave.

💡 My Take

The numbers don't lie: 97% have deployed AI agents, but only 29% see ROI. 68% are "disconnected" from their AI strategy. The market's racing toward $74B in AI MarTech, but most organizations are still figuring out how to make it work. The opportunity isn't in deploying more AI — it's in deploying it systematically. The leaders who bridge this gap will define the next era.
